text: dsh-inner-browser-use 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的浏览器自动化插件：它启动由 agent 管理的独立 Chromium，并将实时画面呈现在当前会话右栏。工具可打开网页、读取正文与控件、点击和输入，也能批量执行带等待条件的操作；还支持查询页面内容、保存截图与媒体，并按名称保存和恢复登录态。适合需要在真实网页中浏览、填写表单或持续使用网站账号的 DSH 用户。使用前需在本机具备 Node.js 20+ 与 Chrome/Chromium；浏览器资料和生成文件保存在本机。

dsh-inner-browser-use adds browser automation to DSH. It runs Chromium and mirrors its live view in the session sidebar. Tools open pages, read content, click, type, run multi-step actions, and save screenshots or named sign-ins. Node.js 20+ and Chrome or Chromium are required locally.
想让 DSH 在独立浏览器里打开网页并操作页面。
有没有办法让 agent 看见我正在浏览的网页画面？
帮我读取网页正文，别把整页控件都塞进结果。
我想让 DSH 自动点击按钮并填写网页表单。
能不能把几步网页操作合成一次调用，还能等页面加载完成？
每次重启都要重新登录网站，怎么保存并恢复账号？
I need an agent to browse and interact with pages in its own Chromium window.
Can DSH read an article and return only the passages relevant to my question?
dsh-inner-browser-use 的功能「独立浏览器」：调用 browser_open 启动或复用独立 Chrome 并打开指定地址，右栏显示当前会话的浏览器画面；登录资料可跨插件重载和 Harness 重启保留。
dsh-inner-browser-use 的功能「按需读取网页」：browser_read 将正文整理为 Markdown，可按问题筛选相关段落；browser_view 则返回可交互控件编号和可见文字，便于后续操作。
dsh-inner-browser-use 的功能「执行网页操作」：agent 可点击控件、输入文本，并通过 browser_do 将多个操作与文本、地址或页面空闲等待条件串成一轮操作。
dsh-inner-browser-use 的功能「保存网站登录」：browser_login 可按名称保存、列出、切换、导入或删除登录；使用时将保存的 Cookie 与本地存储恢复到浏览器并重新打开页面。
dsh-inner-browser-use 会在本机保存浏览器 profile、命名登录资料及截图等产物；登录保险库使用本机 Keychain，无法使用时会回退到权限为 0600 的密钥文件。

dsh-inner-browser-use README · dsh-inner-browser-use：A Chrome that the agent owns, mirrored into the right column of DeepSeek Harness.

The agent opens pages, reads them, clicks, types and scrolls. The browser is a separate
Chrome with its own profile on disk, not the tab the product ships: the column shows a
live picture of that browser, and your own cursor keeps working on the picture.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Tools：| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `browser_open` | Starts the browser (or reuses the running one) and opens an address. `headless: false` shows a real window on the desktop instead. |
| `browser_view` | Returns the address, the title, every control as `1 … 120`, and the visible text. |
| `browser_read` | Reads the page the way a person does: one Markdown block of headings, paragraphs, lists and links, no controls. Far fewer tokens than a snapshot on long pages, and the links stay usable. Give it a `query` and only the sentences that answer it come back: BM25 over Readability-style blocks, then per-sentence scoring with heading, position and link-density priors, idf-weighted coverage, MMR de-duplication and a character budget — 92% fewer tokens on a long page in the bench. A question the page cannot answer returns the nearest passages and says so instead of pasting the page (79% fewer tokens in the bench). When the tab has no answer, the other tabs this chat holds are read in the same call and the answer comes back with the tab it came from — one read instead of switch-and-read-again (90% fewer characters in the bench); `across: false` stay

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Tools：A site you read twice is remembered by origin in `~/.dsh/inner-browser-use/sites.json` (override with `DSH_INNER_BROWSER_STATE_DIR`). After two reads, a site whose page text or control count is big opens in `browser_view` as a `map:` of what is there, and a site whose articles are long has `browser_read` cut at 3,500 characters with a line saying so. Both come with one sentence naming the measurement, and both yield to an explicit `mode`, `query` or `max_chars` — learning changes the default, not the answer to a direct question. `scripts/check-sites.mjs` is the live proof: three views of a 300-button page and three reads of a 12,000-character document, saying where the cut fell.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Tools：`browser_read` on the same page is the words only, in Markdown (measured: 4,520
characters of an about page against 2,987 characters of snapshot — and the
snapshot spends most of its budget on controls; on a long article the gap grows
with the number of controls skipped). `browser_view` answers with one page of text:

```
https://example.com
Example Domain

1 [a] More information

Numbers stay valid until the next read. Anything that changes the page returns a fresh read.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · The column：The pane is a picture of the browser, sent as JPEG over the session's own stream: quality 72,
every frame, about 82 KB and 25 per second on a page at rest. The page is laid out at the size
of the column, so the picture fills the frame instead of sitting letterboxed inside it.

Two pointers live on that picture:

dsh-inner-browser-use README · The column：- **The black arrow** is the agent. It marks where its last click landed, and it moves the
  moment a new one is dispatched, without waiting for the page to repaint.
- **Your cursor** is the real one. Hovering, clicking, the wheel and keystrokes are sent to
  the browser as real mouse and keyboard input, so a site that rejects scripted clicks still
  works. Moving your mouse never moves the black arrow.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · The column：The address row above the picture is an address bar: type an address and press Enter, or use
back, forward and reload. The field follows the page except while you are editing it.

Typing arrives two ways: composed text (Chinese, emoji, anything the input method produces)
lands as one insertion, and keys arrive as themselves, so Backspace deletes one character on
the page.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · The column：The pane opens only in the session that asked for it. A tool call in another session drives
the same browser without taking the column that someone else is reading.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Logins：The profile is a directory of its own: `~/.dsh/inner-browser-use/chrome/default`. It sits
outside the product's browser storage, which is created per process and gone on restart, so a
sign-in here is still there the next day.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Logins：- **Plugin reload.** A reload adopts the Chrome that is still running, with the page it was on.
- **Harness restart.** The same directory is opened again, so cookies, `localStorage` and
  passwords that Chrome saved all survive.
- **Shutdown.** The browser is asked to close rather than killed, which is when Chrome writes
  the last of its cookies.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Borrowing the sign-ins of the Chrome already on this Mac：What starts here is the same Google Chrome binary, only with `--user-data-dir` pointed at the
directory above, so cookies are stored and encrypted exactly the way the Chrome you use every
day stores them — a sign-in can simply be carried over: open the site, then one
`browser_login {action:"import", name:"work"}`. The plugin reads Chrome's cookie store from a
copy (the live file is left alone and Chrome does not have to be closed), opens that site's
cookies with the Chrome Safe Storage key from the keychain, and seals them into its own vault;
`use` puts them back and reopens the page, and they survive restarts.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Borrowing the sign-ins of the Chrome already on this Mac：The profile directory is never shared: Chrome holds a single-instance lock on it, so it cannot be
opened while yours is running, and opening it would rewrite your data across extension and
version differences. Only that site's cookies are carried (localStorage too, when `save` takes
the sign-in) — never the whole profile, and never off this machine.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Borrowing the sign-ins of the Chrome already on this Mac：macOS blocks the read: Chrome's profile is protected, so a direct read is `Operation not
permitted`. Turn on **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access** for DSH. Without
it the tool says so instead of failing quietly.

text:
dsh-inner-browser-use README · What it costs：Measured on the same machine, same fixture, same headless Chrome, against four
others: Playwright MCP, Chrome DevTools MCP, Stagehand and browser-use — all on
their model-free paths, since a model call would only measure inference. Idle RSS
**459–552 MB** (1265–1672), idle CPU **0.03–0.47 %** (36–51 %), a wake in
**0.39–0.59 s** instead of a 4.6–5.1 s restart, and the same page read as **2302
characters** instead of 5662–21396. With six tabs open it is **864–922 MB**, about
+2 MB per tab, still four renderer processes and 0.9 % of a core idle (0.24 % once
the pages settle). A tab on a browser that is already up costs a median of
**42–54 ms** end to end; inside `openTab` the tab start itself is **20 ms**
(24–33 ms for browser-use's raw `new_page`). A screenshot takes **51 ms**, the
same 48–71 ms all four pay — the cost is Chrome's own capture — and what comes
back is a path plus 223 characters instead of the 100–383 KB of base64 they
inline. Cold start is the one place we do not lead: **840 ms** (701–936) against
Stagehand 760 and browser-use 713, because both own Chrome in-process.
`npm run bench` and `npm run tabs` reproduce all of it;

dsh-inner-browser-use README · When nobody is looking：A browser used every two seconds rests after two minutes; one used every ninety seconds waits
nine. The window is p95 of the person's own last 64 gaps, × 6 for rest and × 2 for a reversible
pause, so it is learned rather than configured. Close the column and the rest is one minute
away; leave it open and the page is frozen instead (DOM, scroll and sign-ins kept, screenshot
stream stopped). A wake is 0.3–1.1 s and lands on the same address. `npm run rest` checks the
whole chain headlessly; `docs/RESOURCES.md` has the memory ladder and how the neighbours do it.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · When nobody is looking：Screenshots are the only thing written outside the profile:
`~/.dsh-inner-browser-use/screenshots/`.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Measured：| | |
| --- | --- |
| Navigate to first frame | ~850 ms, network included |
| Frame | 1440×900 JPEG, ~82 KB |
| Stream | ~25 frames per second |
| Pointer move to arrow | 0.8–7 ms |
| Read, dense page | 444 tokens (1510 chars, 90 controls) |
| Read round trip | 1–4 ms |
| Click round trip | 2 ms |
| Key round trip | 7 ms |
| Key to next frame | 15–18 ms |
| Screenshot | 75 ms, 115 KB |

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Install：```bash
git clone https://github.com/regrevia/dsh-inner-browser-use
dsh plugin install /path/to/dsh-inner-browser-use
```

In the app: **Plugins → Install from folder**, and pick the clone. To install the packed
tarball instead, build it from that directory and install the file:

```bash
npm pack                                  # writes dsh-inner-browser-use-0.16.0.tgz
dsh plugin install ./dsh-inner-browser-use-0.16.0.tgz
```

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Install：The plugin appears under **Plugins** as *Background browser*. It needs Google Chrome or
Chromium on the machine; see [docs/COMPATIBILITY.md](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md).

dsh-inner-browser-use README · When it opens：Only when the person asks for it by name: "in the browser", "on the web page",
"open this site", "click it for me". A link on its own is not a request.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · When it opens：- A public article, one link's text, docs, a GitHub repo or PR: read it with
  `web_fetch` or Envoy. No browser, no Chrome process.
- If the page needs a login, is an empty shell to `web_fetch`, or needs a click,
  say why and ask once instead of starting a browser on your own.
- Asked for, it starts without a question and never opens a second, external
  Chrome. The picture stays in this chat's right column and stays open when the
  work is done.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · When it opens：One browser is shared by every chat (see [Sharing](#sharing)), so opening one is
a tab, not a second Chrome.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Use：1. Open the chat you want the agent to browse for.
2. Ask for something on a page: *"open example.com and tell me the title"*.

The first call starts the browser and puts its mirror in this chat's right column. Nothing
opens before a call: a chat that never asked for a page keeps its column as it was.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Sharing：Every chat uses the same background Chrome: one process, one tab per chat, and
each tab's address saved so it can be closed and reopened cheaply. Past six
chats the oldest tab nobody is watching is closed (a watched tab — the one on
someone's screen — never is). Tabs an earlier plugin load left behind are closed
on first use: one profile used for weeks otherwise keeps a renderer per chat that
ever opened it. Nothing is launched per chat, and the browser itself is closed 15
minutes after the last mirror is detached.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Frames, downloads, network：- **Frames are read, including cross-site ones.** Controls inside an iframe are numbered like
  the page's own, whether Chrome shares the page's process or runs the frame apart; a click in
  either lands where the frame actually sits.
- **A download lands on disk.** A click that saves a file writes it into the browser's own
  profile folder, and `browser_downloads` names it, its size and when it arrived.
- **The network is visible.** `browser_network` lists what the page asked for, newest first,
  so a page that fills itself in from an address can be understood without a screenshot.
- **An overlay does not eat the action.** A cookie banner over the button is cleared the way a
  person would clear it, then the click lands — in the same call, and in every step of a
  `browser_do` batch. Anything offering to delete, pay or sign out is reported instead.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · What it does not do：- **It does not touch your Chrome.** The browser runs from a separate profile with no
  connection to the window you are using.
- **The layout viewport is the column, nothing more.** Desktop layout, no mobile emulation, no
touch emulation; a very narrow column is laid out narrow rather than zoomed out.
- **One page at a time.** A link that opens a tab is followed — the mirror lands on the new
  page and the popup closes — so there is never a second page to choose between.

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Compatibility：| | |
| --- | --- |
| Harness | 0.2.0 or newer |
| Chrome | Google Chrome, Chromium or Canary, 112 or newer |
| Runtime | Node 20 or newer |
| License | MIT |

Details in [docs/COMPATIBILITY.md](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md); how the halves connect in
[docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

dsh-inner-browser-use README · Development：```bash
node --test test/*.test.mjs
```

The server half is zero-dependency ESM, the page half is a client module loaded at runtime.
Neither has a build step.
